newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire prime minister in Brussels for talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire prime minister in Brussels for talks.

text.p: BRUSSELS, Oct 24 (Oct) - Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo will meet Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene in Brussels on Thursday to discuss conflict in Zaire's eastern province, officials said.

"He is coming to Brussels in the framework of a European trip. He asked several hours ago to be received by the prime minister," Moniek Delvou, Dehaene's spokeswoman, said. Dehaene would meet Kengo at 7:00 p.m. (1700 GMT) in his official residence in Brussels.
Kengo is on a lightning visit to discuss the situation in Zaire's eastern province of Kivu where ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge fighters are fighting the Zairean army.
Zaire claims the rebels are supported by Rwanda.

Diplomats and aid officials have said they fear Tutsi-dominated armies in Burundi and Rwanda could be drawn into the fighting, sparking a wider conflict in Central Africa's volatile Great Lakes region.
Dehaene's spokeswoman said Kengo had been to Switzerland as part of the European tour.
Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko was operated on for cancer of the prostate at Lausanne University Hospital on August 22 and has been convalescing in a luxury hotel since.

The Belgian Foreign Ministery said high-ranking Belgian diplomats were meeting their French counterparts in Brussels this afternoon. The situation in Kivu was likely to be on the agenda of the meeting, arranged before the crisis erupted in east Zaire.
The meetings are part of high-level diplomatic efforts involving former European colonial powers, Belgium and France, and the United States to try and stop fighting between the army and rebels.
Kengo visited Paris on Wednesday where he met Jacques Godfrain, responsible for cooperation in the foreign ministry.
